description.plain:
Description

The Waveshare Serial Bus Servo Driver Board, model Bus Servo Adapter (A), connects a computer or microcontroller to ST/SC series serial bus servos. This compact bus servo controller integrates power and control circuitry and supports both UART and USB control. It suits custom robotics systems that need servo feedback as well as movement commands.

Depending on the connected servo, the board supports reading angle, load, voltage and operating mode, and programming the servo ID or operating mode. The bus servo driver can theoretically address up to 253 servos, provided the installation has sufficient external power. It is a control adapter rather than a complete robot kit: servos, a power supply and the host computer are separate requirements.

Features

  • ST/SC bus servo control: an interface for compatible serial servos and their feedback.
  • Bus servo host connections: UART for microcontrollers and USB Type-C for suitable computers.
  • A/B mode jumper: position A selects UART; position B selects USB.
  • Two power inputs: a DC5521 jack and screw terminal simplify integration.
  • Programmable IDs and modes: configure servo IDs and servo/motor modes where supported by the connected model.
  • Compact bus servo board: 42 × 33 mm board with 2.5 mm mounting holes.
  • Python, Arduino and Linux libraries for custom bus servo projects.

Specifications

SKU / Model Waveshare-25514 / Bus Servo Adapter (A)
Power Supply DC 9–12.6 V (ST series servo); input voltage must match the servo
Power supply connector 5.5 × 2.1 mm DC
Communication interface UART; USB control through USB Type-C
Dimensions 42.00 × 33.00 mm
Mounting hole size Ø 2.50 mm
Mounting hole spacing 37.00 × 28.00 mm
Compatibility ST/SC series serial bus servos; do not mix the two series
Additional input range 5–8.4 V is also supported according to the documentation when appropriate for the connected servo
Addressable servos Theoretically up to 253, with sufficient external power
Baud rate Must match the connected servos
Additional connections Power screw terminal, UART header, bus servo connectors and A/B jumper
Product-page weight 0.016 kg

Applications

  • Custom robotic arms: control multiple bus servos and inspect position or load feedback.
  • Quadruped and hexapod robots: connect addressable joints through a serial bus.
  • Humanoid prototypes: organize servo IDs and motion routines in a compact installation.
  • Servo test benches: configure individual bus servos and check feedback before mechanical assembly.
  • PC-based bus servo development: use USB to prototype control and telemetry software.
  • Embedded robotics: connect a UART microcontroller for custom closed-loop control experiments.

Product List

  • 1 × Bus Servo Adapter (A)

Other Content

Interface Overview

Dimensions

UART and USB Modes

For UART control, set the jumper to A. The Waveshare wiring guide specifies RX–RX and TX–TX for this adapter, so follow its labeled wiring rather than assuming a generic crossover. For USB control, set the jumper to B and connect a suitable USB cable to the host. Match the baud rate to the connected bus servos.

External Power

The bus servo adapter provides a DC5521 jack and a screw terminal. Select a voltage suitable for every connected servo. The 9–12.6 V range applies to appropriate ST models; SC models may require a lower model-specific supply. Waveshare recommends not mixing ST and SC series. When using different models within one series, verify the voltage requirements and total current demand individually.

Bus Wiring

The pictured servos and cables illustrate a connection and are not included. Assign unique IDs before combining multiple bus servos. The theoretical 253-address limit does not mean one supply can power an arbitrary number of loaded servos.

Resources

  • Bus Servo Adapter (A) documentation
  • UART and USB wiring examples
  • SDKs, examples and hardware resources
  • ST/SC Python control library
  • ST/SC Arduino control library
  • ST/SC Linux control library
  • Bus Servo Adapter (A) schematic
  • STEP mechanical model

FAQ

Which servos does this bus servo driver support?

Compatible ST/SC series serial bus servos. A conventional PWM servo is not a direct substitute. Do not mix ST and SC series together.

Which jumper position should I use?

Use A for UART control and B for USB control, following the corresponding wiring guide.

What supply voltage is required?

Choose a supply rated for the specific servo. 9–12.6 V applies to suitable ST models; the documentation also allows lower model-appropriate voltages.

Can I actually connect 253 servos?

The bus servo driver supports that theoretical address count. Supply capacity, wiring and operating load must all suit the installation.

Are servos and a power supply included?

No. The package contains one adapter board. Servos, a host, cables and external power are separate requirements.

The Waveshare Serial Bus Servo Driver HAT (A) is engineered for controlling up to 253 serial bus servos simultaneously via ESP32 UART or USB port. It serves as a primary controller for robotics projects, supporting both wired and wireless communication. description.plain:
Description

The Waveshare Serial Bus Servo DC buck adapter is a mini step-down power module designed for serial bus servo projects. This compact DC buck adapter accepts a wide DC 9V to 36V input and provides either a 6V or 7.2V regulated output, depending on the selected variant.

Use this compact regulator when a robot, test bench, education kit or servo debugging setup needs cleaner project power without building a separate regulator board. The DC buck adapter is especially useful when the main control board and serial bus servo require a dependable servo-side supply in a small footprint.

The two official variants target different servo voltage needs: the 7.2V DC buck adapter is suitable for servos such as SC15 Servo, while the 6V DC buck adapter is suitable for servos such as SC09 Servo. Choose the output voltage that matches the servo specification and wiring plan.

Features

  • Dedicated servo power accessory: the module is designed for serial bus servo power conversion.
  • Two output options: select the 6V DC buck adapter or the 7.2V DC buck adapter according to the servo model.
  • Wide input range: accepts DC 9V to 36V, making the module flexible for robotics power systems.
  • Mini module design: small board footprint helps keep robot joints, arms, mobile platforms and lab fixtures compact.
  • Easy wiring: onboard DC IN and DC OUT terminals simplify the connection between the supply and servo power rail.
  • Useful with serial bus servos: the 7.2V output is indicated for SC15 Servo, and the 6V output is indicated for SC09 Servo.
  • Project-friendly regulator: the adapter reduces the need for a larger external power board in quick prototypes.

Specifications

Product name Waveshare Serial Bus Servo DC Buck Adapter
Brand Waveshare
Product type Serial bus servo DC-DC buck regulator accessory
Part No. DC BUCK Adapter (6V) / DC BUCK Adapter (7.2V)
Input voltage DC 9V to 36V
Output voltage DC 6V or DC 7.2V, variant dependent
Suitable servo examples 6V version for SC09 Servo; 7.2V version for SC15 Servo
Interface marking DC IN and DC OUT terminals
Use case Power conversion for serial bus servo robotics projects
Official package weight 0.01kg
Shipping weight 10g
Variant SKU Official part Output voltage Official suitable servo example Product list
Waveshare-34860 DC BUCK Adapter (6V) 6V regulated output SC09 Servo DC BUCK Adapter (6V) x1; accessory pack x1
Waveshare-27380 DC BUCK Adapter (7.2V) 7.2V regulated output SC15 Servo DC BUCK Adapter (7.2V) x1; accessory pack x1

Applications

  • Serial bus servo power conversion in robot arms, small mobile robots and servo test rigs.
  • Classroom robotics kits that need a compact DC buck adapter for repeatable servo wiring.
  • Maker-space maintenance benches for SC-series serial bus servo testing.
  • Prototype builds where a DC 9V to 36V input supply must feed a lower-voltage servo rail.
  • Embedded robot projects that need a small DC buck adapter instead of a full custom power board.

Product List

Waveshare-34860 / DC BUCK Adapter (6V): DC BUCK Adapter (6V) x1; accessory pack x1.

Waveshare-27380 / DC BUCK Adapter (7.2V): DC BUCK Adapter (7.2V) x1; accessory pack x1.

Other Content

Variant selection: choose the 6V DC buck adapter for servo systems that specify a 6V rail, and choose the 7.2V DC buck adapter for servo systems that specify a 7.2V rail. Do not select voltage by connector shape alone; always check the servo datasheet or controller documentation first.

Servo connection reference: the official application images show how the DC buck adapter can be connected in serial bus servo projects. Keep polarity and rated voltage aligned with the selected servo model before power-on.

Board reference: the onboard resources and outline images help confirm DC IN, DC OUT and mounting placement before the adapter is installed in a robot chassis or service fixture.

Relevant search terms include DC buck adapter, serial bus servo regulator, 6V servo buck converter, 7.2V servo buck converter, Waveshare servo power module and robot servo power adapter.

Resources

  • Waveshare DC BUCK Adapter wiki

FAQ

What is the difference between the two variants?

The two versions differ by output voltage. Waveshare-34860 is the 6V DC buck adapter, and Waveshare-27380 is the 7.2V DC buck adapter.

What input voltage does the module accept?

The official page lists a DC 9V to 36V input range for this DC buck adapter.

Which servo examples are listed by Waveshare?

Waveshare lists the 7.2V version as suitable for SC15 Servo and the 6V version as suitable for SC09 Servo.

Can I use the adapter with any servo?

Use it only when the servo voltage requirement matches the selected DC buck adapter output. Check the servo documentation before wiring.

Does the package include the adapter only?

The official package section lists one DC BUCK Adapter and an accessory pack for each voltage version.

description.plain:
Description

  • Waveshare 360° Omnidirectional High-Torque 2-Axis Expandable Pan-Tilt Camera Module, Driven by Serial Bus Servos (US)
  • Offers 360° rotation and -45° to 90° tilt range
  • Ensures clear low-light images with LED fill light
  • Supports Raspberry Pi 4B and 5 integration
  • Enables high accuracy with 12-bit magnetic encoder
  • Allows flexible expansion and secondary development

The Waveshare 360° Omnidirectional High-Torque 2-Axis Expandable Pan-Tilt Camera Module, Driven by Serial Bus Servos (US) is a sophisticated device designed for versatile camera control applications. It features a high-torque, two-degree-of-freedom pan-tilt mechanism, driven by serial bus servos, allowing for precise and expansive movement. The module supports a full 360° horizontal rotation and a vertical tilt range from -45° to 90°, making it suitable for a wide array of surveillance and monitoring tasks.

This camera module is compatible with Raspberry Pi 4B and 5, providing seamless integration into existing systems. It is equipped with a 160° ultra wide-angle 5MP camera, ensuring a broad field of view to capture extensive areas. The inclusion of an LED fill light enhances image clarity in low-light conditions, making it ideal for both day and night operations.

The module is built on a general driver board for robots, offering open-source control demonstrations for various functionalities such as photo taking, video recording, face detection, and motion detection. description.plain:
Description

The Waveshare Servo Driver HAT is a 16-channel PWM and servo controller for Raspberry Pi series boards and Jetson Nano. It uses the PCA9685 driver over I2C, so a Raspberry Pi can control many servos while using only two control pins.

This Servo Driver HAT is useful when a project needs stable, repeatable servo signals without relying on software PWM from the Raspberry Pi GPIO. The 12-bit PWM resolution gives 4096 steps per channel, which helps robotic arms, pan-tilt platforms, walkers and small automation fixtures move more smoothly.

The Servo Driver HAT keeps servo power separate through a 5V screw terminal while the board is controlled from the 40-pin GPIO header. Raspberry Pi boards and servos are not included, so it is best treated as a compact expansion board for users who already have the controller board, servos and a suitable 5V servo power supply.

Features

  • 16-channel servo control: drives up to 16 servo or PWM outputs from one Raspberry Pi HAT.
  • PCA9685 driver: dedicated PWM controller reduces timing jitter compared with software-generated PWM.
  • 12-bit PWM resolution: each channel supports 4096 control steps for finer servo positioning.
  • I2C interface: uses only SDA and SCL control lines and leaves more GPIO available for sensors or other modules.
  • 40-pin Raspberry Pi header: standard GPIO extension header supports Raspberry Pi series boards and Jetson Nano.
  • Reserved I2C pins: exposes the I2C control pins for use with other control boards or expansion wiring.
  • External servo power input: screw terminal helps supply the current demanded by multiple servos.

Applications

  • Raspberry Pi robotic arm projects with several servo joints.
  • Hexapod walker, rover steering and pan-tilt camera mechanisms.
  • Education labs that demonstrate PWM, I2C and actuator control.
  • Maker automation fixtures that need repeated servo motion.
  • Jetson Nano robot prototypes that need a compact multi-servo controller.

Connection layout: the Servo Driver HAT plugs into the Raspberry Pi 40-pin header and routes PWM outputs to the servo headers, with an external 5V input for servo power.

Project testing: the official example images show the board driving servos from a Raspberry Pi setup. Use a suitable external servo supply whenever several servos move at the same time.

Mechanical planning: the official demo and dimension resources help verify clearance before adding the board to a robot chassis, classroom fixture or bench prototype.

Are Raspberry Pi boards or servos included?

No. The official package includes the board and screws pack only.

The board provides up to 16 PWM or servo output channels.

Which driver chip does it use?

It uses the PCA9685 PWM controller, controlled through I2C.

Why use this instead of Raspberry Pi GPIO PWM?

The dedicated driver provides stable 12-bit PWM outputs and avoids common software PWM jitter problems.

Does it work with Jetson Nano?

Yes. Waveshare lists support for Raspberry Pi series boards and Jetson Nano.

Description

  • Waveshare General Driver Board, ESP32-Based
  • Versatile and multi-functional, designed for robots
  • Supports WIFI, Bluetooth, and ESP-NOW communications
  • Equipped with onboard motor control and serial bus servos control interfaces
  • Features a 9-axis IMU, TF card slot, and Laser Lidar interface
  • Compatible with Raspberry Pi and Jetson Nano, with open-source demos and tutorials

The Waveshare General Driver Board, ESP32-Based, Supports WIFI, Bluetooth & ESP-NOW is a versatile piece of technology that is compatible with Raspberry Pi and Jetson Nano. This multi-functional driver board is specifically designed for robots, offering a wide range of possibilities. It is built on the ESP32-WROOM-32 module, which supports various forms of wireless communication such as WIFI, Bluetooth, and ESP-NOW.

The board features onboard motor control interfaces that can accommodate either two DC motors with encoders or four DC motors without encoders, divided into two groups. It also includes onboard serial bus servos control interfaces, capable of controlling up to 253 ST3215 serial bus servos and receiving feedback from these servos.

In addition, the board is equipped with an onboard 9-axis IMU, which can provide attitude and heading information at any given time. It supports a power input range of 7~13V and can be powered directly by a 2S or 3S lithium battery module. The board also includes an automatic download circuit for easy program uploading and supports input voltage/current monitoring.

Additional features include an onboard TF card slot, a Laser Lidar interface, and an integrated UART to USB function. The board also has an I2C interface for connecting peripherals such as OLED, IMU, and other I2C devices. It also includes a multi-functional extended header for additional functions, such as controlling servos or relays.

The board comes with a 40-Pin GPIO header for connecting and powering the host computer, such as a Raspberry Pi or Jetson Nano, and can communicate via serial port or I2C. The General Driver Board for Robots also provides open-source demos and detailed tutorials for beginners, making it easy to get started with this technology.

Description

The Waveshare DDSM Driver HAT (B) is a dedicated DDSM400 direct-drive servo motor driver board for building multi-wheel mobile robots. Six motor connectors bring the DDSM400 wiring to one board, while an onboard ESP32-WROOM-32 handles control and wireless communication. This B version is intended for DDSM400 motors; it is not the driver board for DDSM115 or DDSM210.

Power the DDSM400 driver board from a suitable 9–28V supply through its XT60 or DC input, and choose Raspberry Pi UART, USB or the ESP32 wireless interface for control. The board has a 40-pin Raspberry Pi header and an onboard 5V buck converter for Pi power. For a complete drive assembly, pair it with the Waveshare DDSM400 direct-drive servo motor; motors and the external power supply are separate purchases.

Notice: Do not let an unsecured DDSM400 hub motor rotate directly on a desktop; fix its shaft or configure the heartbeat stop function. The DDSM Driver HAT (B) is for DDSM400 motors. Do not mix DDSM115, DDSM210 and DDSM400 motors, as their control commands and feedback differ. Set each motor ID before connecting multiple motors: connect only one motor to the driver board while assigning its ID, or all connected motors may receive the same ID. Choose a power supply with enough current for the connected motors.

Features

  • Six motor ports: connect up to six DDSM400 hub motors to one DDSM400 driver board.
  • Integrated ESP32: ESP32-WROOM-32 supports local control, 2.4GHz Wi-Fi and ESP-NOW wireless operation.
  • Three control paths: Raspberry Pi UART, USB serial control or the ESP32-hosted web interface.
  • Flexible power input: 9–28V through XT60 or 5.5 × 2.5mm DC jack, sized to the motor load.
  • Raspberry Pi interface: 2 × 20-pin header and onboard 5V buck conversion.
  • Accessible setup: controller-selection switch, dual USB-C ports and documented JSON command examples.

Applications

  • Six-wheel robots: bring six DDSM400 wheel motors onto one compact driver board.
  • Raspberry Pi robotics: integrate drive control with a Pi-based navigation or sensing stack.
  • Wireless prototypes: test ESP32 Wi-Fi or ESP-NOW control without a separate wireless controller.
  • USB development: send the documented commands from a computer during bench testing.
  • Educational platforms: compare motor-control interfaces and power distribution in one build.

Other Content

Power and compatibility: this is the DDSM400-specific B board. Do not mix it with DDSM115 or DDSM210 motors. Choose a 9–28V supply with adequate current for the number of connected motors, and disconnect power before changing motor wiring. The listed package does not include DDSM400 motors or a power adapter.

Control selection: use the onboard switch to select the appropriate UART/USB control path. The ESP32 firmware provides documented serial JSON commands at 115200 baud and a Wi-Fi web interface. When connecting a Raspberry Pi, align the 40-pin header and verify the wiring against the Waveshare pin diagram before applying power.

FAQ

Does this driver work with DDSM115 or DDSM210?

No. The DDSM Driver HAT (B) is the DDSM400 version. Select the appropriate A-series board for DDSM115 or DDSM210 instead.

How many motors can I connect?

The DDSM400 driver board provides six DDSM400 motor connectors. Match the external supply capacity to the actual connected motor load.

Are motors and a power supply included?

No. The package contains the board, a 2 × 20-pin header, a USB cable and a screws pack. DDSM400 motors and the 9–28V power supply are sold separately.

Can I control it without a Raspberry Pi?

Yes. The onboard ESP32 and USB interface provide other supported control routes. Follow the Waveshare wiki for mode selection and command examples.
